sahneler.metin: Over a thousand people died on a steamboat close to shore.
Fire spread through the whole ship in minutes.
So why could nobody escape on a boat surrounded by water?
The life preservers were thirteen years old and crumbling.
Some were packed with iron bars to reach the legal weight.
They dragged people under instead of holding them up.
The lifeboats were wired to the deck and would not launch.
The inspector had passed it all. He went to prison.

aciklama:
On June 15, 1904, the steamboat General Slocum burned in New York Harbor. Its life preservers were rotten and weighted with iron; its lifeboats were wired in place.
